title: Joshua Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 12.

questions.question: Who was the king of the Amorites that the children of Israel smote and who dwelt in Heshbon?
questions.correctAnswer: Sihon
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:2 states that Sihon was king of the Amorites and dwelt in Heshbon.

questions.question: According to Joshua 12, from which river to which mountain did the children of Israel possess the land on the other side of Jordan?
options: From the river Arnon unto mount Hermon
From the river Jabbok unto mount Halak
From the sea of Chinneroth unto mount Seir
From the river Jordan unto mount Carmel
questions.correctAnswer: From the river Arnon unto mount Hermon
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:1 specifies the land possessed was from the river Arnon unto mount Hermon.

questions.question: Which king was known to reign in mount Hermon, Salcah, and all Bashan?
questions.correctAnswer: Og
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:5 identifies Og as reigning in mount Hermon, Salcah, and all Bashan.

questions.question: True or False: Moses the servant of the LORD gave the land smitten from the kings on the east side of Jordan to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:6 confirms Moses gave the possession to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half tribe of Manasseh.

questions.question: On which side of Jordan did Joshua and the children of Israel smite kings from Baalgad in the valley of Lebanon to mount Halak?
questions.correctAnswer: West
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:7 describes the kings smitten on the west side of Jordan from Baalgad to mount Halak.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Israel smote only the Amorites and no other nations according to Joshua 12:8.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:8 lists several nations smitten including Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

questions.question: Which city’s king was listed first among the kings smitten on the west side of Jordan?
questions.correctAnswer: Jericho
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:9 lists the king of Jericho first among the kings smitten on the west side of Jordan.

questions.question: True or False: The king of Ai was located beside Bethel according to Joshua 12.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:9 states the king of Ai was beside Bethel.

questions.question: Which king's border was marked by the river Jabbok according to the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Sihon
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:2 states that the river Jabbok was the border of the children of Ammon and was part of Sihon's territory.

questions.question: In Joshua 12, which king was described as being from the remnant of the giants?
questions.correctAnswer: Og
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:4 refers to Og king of Bashan as of the remnant of the giants.

questions.question: Which tribes received the land on the east side of Jordan after Moses and Israel smote the kings?
options: Reubenites, Gadites, half tribe of Manasseh
questions.correctAnswer: Reubenites, Gadites, half tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:6 confirms these tribes received the possession on the east side of Jordan.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua and the children of Israel smote kings in the mountains, valleys, plains, springs, wilderness, and south country on the west side of Jordan.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:8 lists all these places where kings were smitten on the west side of Jordan.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT mentioned as a nation whose kings were smitten on the west side of Jordan?
questions.correctAnswer: Philistines
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:8 lists the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, but not Philistines.

questions.question: In Joshua 12, which king's territory extended from the middle of the river Arnon and included half Gilead?
questions.correctAnswer: Sihon
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:2 describes Sihon's rule from Aroer on the bank of Arnon and half Gilead.

questions.question: Sequence question: Which event occurred first according to Joshua 12?
options: Joshua smiting kings on the west side of Jordan
Division of land to tribes on the west side
Listing of kings on the west side
questions.correctAnswer: Moses smiting Sihon and Og
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:6 shows Moses and Israel smote Sihon and Og before Joshua smote kings on the west side (Joshua 12:7).

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Which two kings ruled cities located beside Bethel according to Joshua 12?
options: The king of Ai and the king of Bethel
The king of Jerusalem and the king of Hebron
The king of Makkedah and the king of Bethel
The king of Debir and the king of Geder
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Ai and the king of Bethel
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:9 mentions the king of Ai as being beside Bethel, and Joshua 12:16 mentions the king of Bethel. Both cities are adjacent as per these verses.

questions.question: How does the list of kings in Joshua 12:10-11 teach about God's provision for the tribes of Israel?
options: God gave them victory over many kings including Jerusalem and Hebron
God commanded them to avoid these cities
God punished them through these kings
God instructed them to make peace with these kings
questions.correctAnswer: God gave them victory over many kings including Jerusalem and Hebron
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:10-11 lists kings like Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, and Lachish who were defeated and whose lands were given to Israel (Joshua 12:7), showing God's provision through conquest.

questions.question: Which two kings ruled neighboring cities mentioned in Joshua 12:12-13?
options: The king of Eglon and the king of Gezer
The king of Debir and the king of Geder
The king of Hormah and the king of Arad
The king of Libnah and the king of Adullam
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Debir and the king of Geder
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:13 names the king of Debir and the king of Geder consecutively, indicating neighboring kings conquered by Israel.

questions.question: True or False: The king of Hormah and the king of Arad ruled cities within the land taken by Israel according to Joshua 12.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:14 lists the king of Hormah and the king of Arad as among those defeated and whose lands were given to Israel.

questions.question: According to Joshua 12:15, what does the inclusion of kings such as Libnah and Adullam teach about Israel’s conquest?
options: Israel conquered a wide variety of city-states including Libnah and Adullam
Israel avoided conflicts with these cities
These cities were allies of Israel
These cities were outside the promised land
questions.correctAnswer: Israel conquered a wide variety of city-states including Libnah and Adullam
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:15 lists these kings among those defeated, indicating Israel’s thorough conquest of the promised land.

questions.question: What practical lesson about obedience and trust in God can be drawn from the list of kings conquered by Israel in Joshua 12:16?
options: Obedience to God's commands leads to victory over obstacles as shown by conquering Makkedah and Bethel
Trusting in human strength is sufficient for success
Avoiding conflict is the best way to live
Faith has no impact on earthly struggles
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's commands leads to victory over obstacles as shown by conquering Makkedah and Bethel
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:16, like the verses before it, shows that Israel’s obedience and trust in God resulted in defeating these kings and possessing their lands, reinforcing the value of faith-driven action.

questions.question: Which king was NOT mentioned in the list from Joshua 12:9-16?
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Hazor
questions.explanation: While the king of Hazor is mentioned later in Joshua 12:19, he is not included in the list of kings from verses 9 through 16, which focus on different cities.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 12:9-16 emphasizes the comprehensive nature of Israel's conquest, covering kings in mountains, valleys, and plains.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:7-8 describes Israel’s conquest in diverse terrains, and the detailed list of kings in verses 9-16 shows the extent of territory and variety of locations conquered.

questions.question: How does Joshua 12:9-10 demonstrate the virtue of humility in the context of Israel's conquests?
options: By showing that even great cities like Jerusalem were conquered through God's power, teaching reliance on Him rather than self
By boasting about Israel's military strength
By encouraging pride in the defeated kings
questions.correctAnswer: By showing that even great cities like Jerusalem were conquered through God's power, teaching reliance on Him rather than self
questions.explanation: The defeat of significant cities such as Jerusalem (Joshua 12:10) reminds believers that victory comes through dependence on God, fostering humility rather than pride.

questions.question: What does Joshua 12:11-12 reveal about the importance of integrity in leadership and obedience to God?
options: Kings like Jarmuth and Lachish were defeated because they opposed God’s plan, highlighting the need for godly leadership
These kings led Israel to victory
Integrity was not important in these battles
The kings were rewarded for their faith
questions.correctAnswer: Kings like Jarmuth and Lachish were defeated because they opposed God’s plan, highlighting the need for godly leadership
questions.explanation: The defeat of these kings in Joshua 12:11-12 underscores the consequences of opposing God's will and the biblical call for integrity aligned with God’s commands.

questions.question: A fellow believer is struggling with trusting God to overcome obstacles. Based on Joshua 12:13-14, what biblical truth can you share?
options: God grants victory over strong enemies when His people obey and trust Him, as seen with kings like Debir and Hormah being conquered
Success depends solely on human effort
Avoidance of conflict is always best
God does not intervene in battles
questions.correctAnswer: God grants victory over strong enemies when His people obey and trust Him, as seen with kings like Debir and Hormah being conquered
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:13-14 lists defeated kings, showing that trusting God and obedience lead to overcoming formidable challenges.

questions.question: True or False: The repeated phrase 'one' after each king’s name in Joshua 12:9-16 highlights that Israel defeated many individual kings rather than multiple kings ruling the same city.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Each verse from Joshua 12:9 through 12:16 mentions 'one' after each king, emphasizing that Israel defeated individual kings ruling distinct cities.

questions.question: According to Joshua 12:15-16, what lesson about generosity and sharing can be drawn from God giving the conquered lands to different tribes?
options: God’s provision is to be shared fairly among His people, as lands were divided among tribes like those of Libnah, Adullam, Makkedah, and Bethel
Some tribes received all the land
The land was kept by a single king
The tribes competed for land without God’s guidance
questions.correctAnswer: God’s provision is to be shared fairly among His people, as lands were divided among tribes like those of Libnah, Adullam, Makkedah, and Bethel
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:7 and 12:15-16 show that the lands conquered from these kings were distributed according to tribal divisions, teaching fairness and generosity.

questions.question: What does Joshua 12:9-10 promise will happen if the Israelites continue to obey God’s commands as in earlier chapters?
options: They will continue to possess the land and defeat their enemies, including kings like Jericho and Jerusalem
They will lose the land to their enemies
They will be scattered among nations
They will be ignored by their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They will continue to possess the land and defeat their enemies, including kings like Jericho and Jerusalem
questions.explanation: The list of defeated kings in Joshua 12:9-10 demonstrates the result of obedience—continued possession and victory over enemies as promised in earlier chapters.

questions.question: How does Joshua 12:11-12 encourage believers to apply prayer in facing challenges today?
options: Believers should seek God’s guidance and help as Israel did to overcome kings like Jarmuth and Gezer
Believers should rely only on their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should seek God’s guidance and help as Israel did to overcome kings like Jarmuth and Gezer
questions.explanation: The success over these kings (Joshua 12:11-12) was possible because Israel trusted and followed God’s leadership, encouraging prayerful dependence.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 12.

questions.question: Which kings did Joshua and the children of Israel smite on this side of Jordan, from Baalgad in the valley of Lebanon to mount Halak?
options: Kings of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites
questions.correctAnswer: Kings of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:7-8 lists the kings on this side of Jordan whom Joshua and Israel smote, including the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

questions.question: Who was the king of the Amorites, dwelling in Heshbon, whose territory extended from the river Arnon to the river Jabbok?
questions.correctAnswer: Sihon
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:2 identifies Sihon as the king of the Amorites dwelling in Heshbon with rule extending from the river Arnon to the river Jabbok.

questions.question: True or False: Og king of Bashan was described as one of the remnant of the giants.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:4 clearly states that Og king of Bashan was of the remnant of the giants.

questions.question: Which tribes received possession of the land smitten from Sihon and Og?
options: Reubenites, Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh
questions.correctAnswer: Reubenites, Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:6 states Moses gave the land to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh after smiting Sihon and Og.

questions.question: Which king ruled from mount Hermon and all Bashan, including Salcah?
questions.correctAnswer: Og
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:5 specifies that Og reigned in mount Hermon, Salcah, and all Bashan.

questions.question: True or False: The king of Jericho was one of the kings smitten by Joshua and Israel on this side of Jordan.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:9 lists the king of Jericho as one of the kings smitten by Joshua and Israel.

questions.question: Which king mentioned in Joshua 12 ruled near Bethel?
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Ai
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:9 mentions the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel.

questions.question: Which pair of kings ruled cities located along the coastal region as mentioned in Joshua 12?
options: The king of Dor and the king of the nations of Gilgal
The king of Hebron and the king of Jerusalem
The king of Ai and the king of Bethel
The king of Taanach and the king of Megiddo
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Dor and the king of the nations of Gilgal
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:23 identifies the king of Dor in the coast of Dor and the king of the nations of Gilgal as coastal rulers.

questions.question: Which king ruled in the city of Megiddo according to Joshua 12?
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Megiddo
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:21 explicitly mentions the king of Megiddo among the kings defeated.

questions.question: Which king ruled the city of Tirzah, the last city mentioned among the kings defeated?
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Tirzah
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:24 names the king of Tirzah as the last among the thirty-one kings defeated.

questions.question: Which king ruled in the city of Hazor, a significant Canaanite city defeated by Joshua?
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Hazor
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:19 lists the king of Hazor as one of the kings defeated.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word for 'smite' as used in Joshua 12, and how does it emphasize the conquest theme?
options: To strike down decisively, indicating total defeat
questions.correctAnswer: To strike down decisively, indicating total defeat
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'smite' (נָכָה - nakah) used in Joshua 12 means to strike down decisively, emphasizing the total military conquest over the kings listed (Joshua 12:1-24).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of Israel's possession of land after defeating kings as described in Joshua 12?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 2:24-37
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 2:24-37 recounts Israel's victories over Sihon and Og, echoing Joshua 12's theme of conquest and land possession.

questions.question: How does the literary device of listing thirty-one kings in Joshua 12 function in the narrative?
options: It serves as an inclusio framing Israel's complete conquest
It is a random enumeration with no narrative purpose
It is a poetic parallelism celebrating kingship
It foreshadows the division of the kingdom of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It serves as an inclusio framing Israel's complete conquest
questions.explanation: The detailed list of thirty-one kings in Joshua 12 acts as an inclusio, framing the narrative by emphasizing the completeness of Israel's conquest (Joshua 12:24).

questions.question: Which king ruled at Jokneam of Carmel as per Joshua 12?
options: The king of Jokneam of Carmel
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Jokneam of Carmel
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:22 explicitly mentions the king of Jokneam of Carmel among the defeated kings.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which king ruled from Aroer by the river Arnon and was defeated by Moses and the children of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Sihon king of the Amorites
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:2 identifies Sihon king of the Amorites as ruling from Aroer by the river Arnon and being defeated by Moses and Israel.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is demonstrated by Moses giving the conquered lands to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh?
options: Doctrine of Divine Sovereignty in election
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of God's covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:6 shows Moses giving the land as a possession to the tribes, illustrating God's faithfulness to His covenant promises to Israel regarding the land.

questions.question: According to Joshua 12:4-5, the king Og of Bashan was notable for what characteristic?
options: He was one of the remnant of the giants
He was a peaceful king who made treaties
He ruled only a small territory
He was the first king defeated by Joshua
questions.correctAnswer: He was one of the remnant of the giants
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:4 describes Og king of Bashan as being of the remnant of the giants, highlighting God's victory over formidable enemies.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by the comprehensive defeat of thirty-one kings on the west side of Jordan as listed in Joshua 12:7-24?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: The conquest of many kings across diverse territories (Joshua 12:7-24) reveals God's omnipotence in delivering Israel and establishing His promises.

questions.question: What does the listing of various kings defeated by Israel in Joshua 12 teach about God’s justice in the conquest?
options: God enacts righteous judgment on nations opposing His people
God arbitrarily destroys nations without cause
The kings surrendered willingly without conflict
The conquest was purely political with no divine involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God enacts righteous judgment on nations opposing His people
questions.explanation: The detailed enumeration of kings defeated (Joshua 12:1-24) illustrates God's just judgment against those who opposed His covenant people.

questions.question: How does Joshua 12:9-14 contribute to the broader redemptive narrative of Israel’s possession of the Promised Land?
options: It shows the fulfillment of God's promise to give land to Israel
It depicts Israel's failure to conquer Canaan
It introduces a new covenant with the Amorites
It records Israel's exile from the land
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the fulfillment of God's promise to give land to Israel
questions.explanation: The listing of kings defeated (Joshua 12:9-14) demonstrates the fulfillment of God’s promise to Abraham regarding possession of Canaan.

questions.question: What synthesis of doctrine is seen in Joshua 12:2-3 and Joshua 12:4-5 regarding God’s victory and the nature of Israel’s conquest?
options: God’s justice in judging wicked nations and His faithfulness in granting the land
Human military skill is the primary cause of Israel’s success
Conquest is unrelated to God’s promises or justice
The kings defeated were all righteous but lost by chance
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice in judging wicked nations and His faithfulness in granting the land
questions.explanation: Verses 2-3 describe Sihon’s extensive territory conquered for Israel, while 4-5 describe Og’s defeat, collectively showing God’s righteous judgment and faithful land grant.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by His giving the land as a possession to Israel through Moses and Joshua as seen in Joshua 12:6 and 12:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:6 and 12:7 show Moses and Joshua giving the land to Israel, revealing God’s faithfulness in fulfilling His promises.

questions.question: How does Joshua 12:23-24 emphasize the completeness of Israel’s conquest on the west side of Jordan?
options: By listing the king of Tirzah as the last of thirty-one kings defeated
By describing ongoing battles after these kings
By mentioning only a few kings defeated
By stating that Israel did not fully possess the land
questions.correctAnswer: By listing the king of Tirzah as the last of thirty-one kings defeated
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:23-24 concludes the chapter by enumerating all thirty-one kings defeated, showing the thoroughness of Israel’s conquest.

questions.question: What apologetic response does Joshua 12:1-24 provide against the claim that Israel’s conquest was mere myth or exaggeration?
options: It provides a detailed historical record of kings defeated and territories possessed
It admits that the conquest never occurred
It attributes the conquest to natural disasters
It remains silent on the conquest details
questions.correctAnswer: It provides a detailed historical record of kings defeated and territories possessed
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:1-24 meticulously lists defeated kings and conquered lands, supporting the historicity of Israel’s conquest against sceptical claims.

questions.question: What does the defeat of Og king of Bashan (Joshua 12:4-5) typologically foreshadow in Christological terms?
options: Christ’s victory over the spiritual giants (powers) opposing God’s kingdom
Christ’s earthly reign as king of Bashan
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s victory over the spiritual giants (powers) opposing God’s kingdom
questions.explanation: Og, a giant king defeated by God’s people (Joshua 12:4-5), foreshadows Christ’s ultimate triumph over spiritual enemies (Ephesians 6:12).

questions.question: What does Joshua 12:8 teach about the diversity of peoples defeated, and what theological implication does this have for God’s plan of redemption?
options: God’s plan involves judgment on various nations opposing His covenant
Only one ethnic group was defeated
God’s judgment was limited to Amorites only
The defeated peoples were allies of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God’s plan involves judgment on various nations opposing His covenant
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:8 lists multiple peoples (Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, etc.) defeated, showing God's sovereign judgment on diverse opposition to His redemptive plan.

questions.question: How does the combined teaching of Joshua 12:6 and Joshua 12:24 demonstrate the doctrine of God’s sovereign election and covenant fulfillment?
options: God sovereignly elects Israel to possess the land and faithfully fulfills His covenant promises
The land was taken by human effort alone without divine involvement
God’s covenant is conditional on Israel’s perfection
Israel’s possession was temporary and unfulfilled
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly elects Israel to possess the land and faithfully fulfills His covenant promises
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:6 shows God giving land possession, and 12:24 lists the defeated kings, confirming God’s sovereign election and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: According to Joshua 12:10-13, what does the defeat of the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, and Lachish reveal about God's plan for the central hill country?
options: God intended to establish Israel’s dominion over the strategically important central highlands
God allowed these kings to remain in power
The central hill country was given to other nations
These cities were spared from conquest
questions.correctAnswer: God intended to establish Israel’s dominion over the strategically important central highlands
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:10-13 lists kings in the mountainous region defeated, showing God’s purpose to secure Israel’s control over key central territories.

questions.question: What synthesis of Joshua 12:1 and Joshua 12:7 reveals about the geographical scope of Israel’s conquest under Moses and Joshua?
options: The conquest spanned both east and west of Jordan, fulfilling God’s promise of land possession
The conquest was limited only to the east side of Jordan
Conquest was only symbolic and not territorial
Moses and Joshua failed to conquer any territory
questions.correctAnswer: The conquest spanned both east and west of Jordan, fulfilling God’s promise of land possession
questions.explanation: Joshua 12:1 describes conquest east of Jordan; 12:7 describes conquest west of Jordan, showing the comprehensive fulfillment of God’s promise.
